title: Getting Singapore to be a Sporting Nation
what_it_is: Getting Singapore to be a Sporting Nation

sections.label: Minister on delayed Olympic broadcast
sections.summary: Six days before the opening ceremony, the Minister reiterated that watching a delayed broadcast would be a different way of celebrating.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Sunday before the start of the Olympics, that is, 31 July, which was six days before the opening ceremony, our Minister reiterated that watching a delayed broadcast would be a different way of celebrating.

sections.label: Pooling resources for live broadcasts
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MCCY, Mediacorp, cable operators and telcos pool resources, negotiate early and budget to guarantee live broadcasts of major sporting events.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: An opportunity to unite the nation should not be left to a commercial decision.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that in future, the relevant bodies: the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), Mediacorp, cable television operators and telecommunications companies can pool their resources together and prepare their negotiations far ahead of time and allocate the budget to ensure we are guaranteed a contract to broadcast major sporting events "live", including all major games that our athletes are taking part in.

sections.label: NS deferment for Olympic athletes
sections.summary: MINDEF changed its policy to let Joseph Schooling and Quah Zheng Wen defer NS till end-August 2016, but deferment remains ad hoc and case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Evidently, Singaporeans do consider our athletes' abilities to represent our country to be important.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I appreciate that after three years of debate in this House and after many appeals from the parents and the National Sports Associations, MINDEF changed its policy to let Joseph Schooling and Quah Zheng Wen defer their NS till end-August 2016.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But still, deferment is ad hoc and only on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I think MINDEF and MCCY could have done better in supporting our Olympic-bound athletes.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They should work together to come up with a policy for our sportsmen so that it is transparent, and everyone can be clear about what they can expect and what standards they have to achieve in order to pursue their career in the sporting world.

sections.label: Ang Peng Siong on Olympic cycles
sections.summary: Ang Peng Siong said in a recent interview that one would need at least two Olympic cycles or more to realise their Olympic dream.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As Ang Peng Siong mentioned in his recent interview, one would need at least two Olympic cycles or even more in order to realise their Olympic dream.

sections.label: Funding athletes with potential
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government can set aside more funding to tailor-make programmes for athletes with potential, such as longer overseas attachments.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A lot of people know that May and Colin Schooling spent more than $1 million on Joseph Schooling.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While the spexScholarship supports elite athletes and para-athletes, can the 	Page: 110 Government do more?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can we set aside more funding so that we can tailor-make programmes for those athletes who show potential?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can send athletes with potential overseas for longer term attachment, for example, one to two years in Bolles School in the United States (US) for swimmers.

sections.label: Support for Paralympians and para-athletes
sections.summary: Support for Paralympians shows the disabled they are valued, and the speaker hopes improvements apply to para-athletes and more para-athletes are sought.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the same time, our support for the Paralympians shows the disabled that they are valued members of our community.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, while we look into how to improve support for our athletes, I hope any improvements will also apply to para-athletes and that we keep looking for more para-athletes by encouraging disabled people to pursue sports.

sections.label: Sports support system funding
sections.summary: The system provides grants, training, coaching, sports medicine and personal development, spending S$60 million over five years and close to S$90 million yearly, supporting over 1,500 carded athletes in over 40 sports.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The system offers comprehensive support from financial grants, training and coaching, sports medicine to personal development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will spend a total of S$60 million over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: And if we include funding and support given to NSAs and all Team Singapore athletes, we would be investing close to S$90 million per year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The system supports athletes of varying potential and development needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: There are currently over 1,500 carded athletes, including our para-athletes, covering over 40 sports.

sections.label: spexScholarship scheme elite athletes
sections.summary: The spexScholarship scheme, introduced in 2013, lets elite athletes train full-time; there are 69 spexScholars, 14 qualifying for the Olympics and seven for the Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We also introduced the spexScholarship scheme in 2013 to enable our elite athletes with the potential to excel at the highest level to focus on training full-time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: There are 69 spexScholars at present; 14 of them qualified for the Olympics and seven for the Paralympics.

sections.label: Mediacorp Olympics broadcast rights cost
sections.summary: Mediacorp paid about US$2.5 million for 2012 London Olympics broadcast rights and was quoted almost three times that for the Rio Olympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: You may have read from the media that Mediacorp paid about US$2.5 million for broadcast rights to the 2012 London Olympics and was quoted almost three times that for the Rio Olympics.

sections.label: spexBusiness network athlete opportunities
sections.summary: The spexBusiness network has 33 businesses offering opportunities to athletes, and more than 80 athletes have benefited.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our spexBusiness network has 33 businesses offering opportunities to our athletes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: More than 80 athletes have benefited from this programme.

sections.label: MINDEF NS deferment for sportsmen
sections.summary: MINDEF grants exceptional sportsmen long-term NS deferment based on meeting sporting goals and agreed performances, and has extended Schooling's deferment to 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: MINDEF has granted exceptional sportsmen long-term deferment from NS, on the basis of them meeting sporting goals and agreed performances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: And MINDEF has announced that Schooling's deferment has been extended to 2020.

sections.label: NS deferment matrix for athletes
sections.summary: A matrix tracks athletes' progress and milestones, and in Schooling's case a deferment would have been given regardless of gold, silver or bronze.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: For example, if they have already qualified for the Olympics, can we allow them to decide how long they want to defer their NS so long as maybe we fix the age limit?

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Indeed, there is a matrix, and the matrix actually tracks the progress of athletes through time and also established milestones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In the case of Schooling, I think whether he medalled with a gold, silver or bronze, he would have gotten a deferment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, indeed, there is an established matrix and information will be given to the athletes at an appropriate time.
